origin_result.basis: The origin calculator requires a bill of materials (each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency) and a declaration (product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, operations done in the UAE). No checks were performed due to missing data.

procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae); the factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and obtain a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online, and submit the application. Processing takes about one working day.

The certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from the date of issue, covers one import (may list several products), and must be issued prior to, at, or within 5 working days of the date of exportation. It bears the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority.

The application must include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately. The issuing authority may apply risk management, including requesting detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.

The exporter must ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage. If a third-party invoice is used, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue. India may request verification; the UAE authority answers within 90 days (extendable by 60). Refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying the preference.
Pay the certificate-of-origin fee, which ranges from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on the invoice value in AED (fee bands per Cabinet Resolution 208/2025).

caveats.note: CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping, countervailing, or safeguard duties still apply.

The CEPA rate reduces BCD and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS, and anti-dumping/countervailing/safeguard duties still apply. A lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount because IGST is levied on a base that includes BCD.
The '+' in the product-specific rule is interpreted as 'and' (both the tariff shift and the value-addition test must pass); this is Mansha's interpretation as the agreement does not define '+'.

Value addition may be calculated by build-down or build-up; 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement. Whether the two methods share one threshold is not stated beyond the 5-percentage-point Ex-Works reduction.
Non-originating materials are valued at their customs (CIF) value at import; if unknown, at the first ascertainable price paid in the UAE or India.
Minimal operations listed in Article 3.5 (e.g., simple cutting, simple assembly, repacking, labelling) never confer origin, even if the product-specific rule is met.
De minimis tolerance allows up to 10% of the FOB value or Ex-Works price to be non-originating material; for wholly obtained products the limit is 1%.
Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in UAE production may count as originating, but the last production process in the UAE must go beyond minimal operations.

A certificate of origin may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks) of India's certificate form. Minor typing errors are tolerated; discrepancies in signature or seal are not.
Certificate fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is performed by Mansha.
Factory Registration requires the factory to be outside a free zone; free-zone producers are likely not eligible for CEPA certificates (inference, confirm with Ministry of Economy and Tourism).

The Indian importer must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including the origin criterion claimed, keep supporting documents for at least 5 years, and respond to customs requests within 10 working days. Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed, seen only in secondary sources).

No official page names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically; its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page remains on moet.gov.ae.
